_schema.units: model units; world size = modelSize * scale (uniform). glTF axes: +Y up, front (camera side at yaw 0) = +Z.
_schema.depth: world units of the model ORIGIN below the gameplay plane (three: y = -depth). topClearance = depth - worldSize.y / 2 (keep > ~650 so nothing pokes through the debris layers at 420-620).
_schema.visibleWithin: where the landmark is on screen, as its anchor minus the camera target on the plane (+x east, +y north = screen up): dy range through dx 0, dx range at dy = centreDy (the offset at which it sits mid-screen = depth / tan 55 = 0.70 x depth). The view footprint at depth D is centred 0.70 D NORTH of the target, about +-0.95 D wide and +-0.7 D deep: a deep landmark shows while it lies ahead (north) of the player and slides out at the bottom once the player passes over it. default = camera distance 48, max = 210; pitch 55, vFOV 50, 16:9.
_schema.haze: suggested mix toward the zone haze colour (zoneLook haze): albedo / emissive share. Do not apply the full depth-layer haze (0.8+) - the emissive accents must survive.
_schema.glows: optional additive sprites (vfx/glow_soft.png) at the glow_<i> empties; size in world units.
_schema.nodes: child nodes: *_Beacons / *_Lights blink, *_Glyphs pulse emission, Forge_Ring spins.

landmarks.where: 1 instance at radius 900-1200 from home at a seeded angle in the eastern half (-70..+70 deg from east): the gas-giant compass sits north-west, so the two never overlap on screen and the player gets two bearings
landmarks.emissive: Relay_Beacons: crown ring of 6 red lamps (blink 1 s, staggered), green/red wing tips (nav), amber top lamp (slow 2.5 s pulse) and 3 red antenna tips; warm window ring on the hub stays lit (baked in the root). glow_0 = amber halo at the top lamp.

landmarks.where: 3 shards of the same broken ring: radius 2400-3200, angles 120 deg apart + seeded jitter (+-25 deg); give each a different yaw so they read as different pieces
landmarks.emissive: Shard_Lights: ~20 pirate red lamps on both rim walls + one on the snapped spoke tip - blink irregularly (0.6-1.4 s, random phase), let a few stay dark. Root: three districts of warm windows (pirate squats, window_warm) among dim dead ones (der_window) on the habitat floor. glow_0/1 = warm halos over the two big lit districts, glow_2 = red halo on the spoke tip.

landmarks.where: 4 walls at radius 5000-7200, angles 90 deg apart + seeded jitter; avoid the nebula cores (radiation sources) - a wall reads best a little off a core, never on it
landmarks.emissive: Crystals use the violet gradient swatches (emissive root -> pale tip) with bright violet edge seams on the tallest prisms (tier_glow_cr); the cleft between the two rows is a glowing teal blade (reactor_glow) peeking between the crystals = the inner glow; teal fissures in the root ridge. glow_0..2 = teal halos along the cleft (slow 4-6 s breathing, out of phase), glow_3 = violet halo at the crown.

landmarks.where: 2 instances at radius 9000-11000 on opposite sides (seeded angle); it is the "Vyhasnutie" memorial of the star-smiths - keep it clear of workshops so it is never mistaken for one
landmarks.emissive: Cinder: ember crack network (ember 1.8, a few hot kov_ember 4.0) baked in the root. Forge_Glyphs: long-short-short ember dashes on the claw ribs - slow dying pulse (6-8 s, intensity 0.4-1.0). Forge_Ring: spin around local +Y, ~0.01 rad/s. glow_0 = big dim ember halo behind the cinder (size ~1.6x the sphere).

reuse.rings: models/planets/gas_giant_rings.glb (radii 1.28-2.35 planet radii, tilt with the planet)

landmarks.where: WORLD-ANCHORED (not camera-following) at home + (-1150, +2270) (sim x, y; +y = north = screen up), depth 2500: at home it sits exactly where the current backdrop puts it (upper left, zoneLook offset (-1150, 520) + the 0.70 x depth look-ahead), and it stays on screen from anywhere in ring 1 while sliding with true parallax - flying toward home moves it toward its home position. Today ZoneEnvironment keeps it at a fixed screen offset with a saturating parallax lag (PARALLAX_LIMIT 1600) and keepOffCenter(), so it cannot work as a compass; the small moon can stay camera-following.

echoColumn.mesh: unit column: 3 crossed quads through the axis, width 1 (x), height 2 (glTF y -1..1), origin = the beacon; UV u across (core at u 0.5), v along (beacon at v 0.5, the top end samples the top row of the image). Own material AF_EchoColumn (not the atlas, texture embedded).
echoColumn.note: Place at the Ozvena beacon (ozvena_beacon.glb origin) scaled (14, 700, 14): the column runs 700 u up and 700 u down. Rising toward the camera it is seen as a long ray from far away even when the beacon is off-screen; the downward half shows when the beacon is north of the view. Render additive, unlit, no depth write, double-sided (or rotate one quad around Y to face the camera and drop the other two). Fade it out when the camera is within ~60 u horizontally of the beacon (else the beam passes the camera) and pulse it with the Kovaci rhythm (long-short-short, 1.6 s) by modulating the colour; optionally scroll a brightness band up along v. Hide for undiscovered Echoes or show only after the first signal fix (design choice). GEOMETRY: with the 55 deg camera vertical lines converge to vanishing points just above / below the frame, so a VERTICAL column only reaches the screen for beacons ahead (north, the down-ray crosses the view) or within ~2 screen widths; beacons far east/west or south stay invisible. COMPASS option (tiltDeg.compass): rotate the column about three.js X by +35 deg (= 90 - pitch; the top leans toward the camera, the lower half points down-north along the view direction) and draw only the lower half (v < 0.5): the down-ray then converges on the screen centre from ANY beacon in front of the camera - every Echo shoots a ray that enters from its side of the screen and points at the ship (preview landmark-echo_column-compass.png).
